translate_en|mods/MaskaradsSummerCar/42/: <type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD XIV^CABIN CLIMATE<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_climate_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Cabin climate is tied to the engine. Heater uses warm coolant; A/C needs compressor and belt, so comfort can fail because of circulation or accessory problems.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Use normal heater and A/C controls. Heater works only with warm, sufficient, clean coolant plus a working heater core, pump, and fan belt; A/C needs compressor and belt and becomes stronger at higher engine speed. The blower consumes battery even with engine off. Climate failure removes comfort, not the ability to drive.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD X^COMPONENT CLASSES<type:text, x:105, y:260, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Standard, Heavy-Duty, and Sport are fit classes, not a straight upgrade ladder. A different class can save a found car, but later costs extra wear through compatibility stress.<type:text, x:105, y:460, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:510, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Read the class before installing a part: Standard, Heavy-Duty, and Sport are compatibility classes, not upgrades. A matching class preserves intended output. A mismatched part still installs, but causes extra wear, heat, fuel use, and stress in linked systems; Diagnostics reports this stress.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD IV^COOLING SYSTEM<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_cooling_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Cooling is one loop: radiator stores liquid, pump circulates it, thermostat directs flow, and fan and belt move heat away. One healthy part cannot save a broken loop.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>In Components, monitor the radiator, water pump, thermostat, fan, hoses, and fan belt as one cooling loop. Low or contaminated coolant, leaks, or a broken belt or pump reduce cooling; heat then damages engine parts and may stop the engine. Replace failed parts and restore correct coolant before driving under load.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD I^OIL DIAGNOSTICS<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_dipstick_sketch_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>A dipstick reads what is happening inside a closed engine without dismantling it. It is a diagnostic tool: oil condition affects pressure and protection of internal components.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Keep an oil dipstick in your inventory, then open vehicle mechanics and select Fluids. It reveals oil cleanliness and freshness plus coolant and transmission-fluid quality; fluid amount and type remain visible without it. The dipstick only diagnoses—it does not refill or clean a system.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD XII^DRIVING UNDER LOAD<type:text, x:105, y:260, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Overload is not just fast driving: it occurs when the engine requests high power without accelerating the car for too long. That heats vulnerable engine and drivetrain components and accelerates wear.<type:text, x:105, y:460, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:510, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>When high RPM and throttle do not produce acceleration, release throttle or regain speed. Sustained bogging, drivetrain slip, and heavy load build overload after a short grace period; it increases heat and wear in engine and drivetrain parts until normal driving lets it recover. An installed ECU marks overload in Diagnostics.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD XI^ECU DIAGNOSTICS<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_ecu_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>The ECU does not repair a vehicle. It makes hidden simulation data readable, helping separate oil-pressure, cooling, traction, and overload causes.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>In Components → Diagnostics, install a Vehicle ECU from inventory with the hood open and engine stopped. It unlocks the Diagnostics tab and replaces handheld checks with all fluid-quality and temperature readings. Use its live negative-effects list to separate oil-pressure, cooling, drivetrain, compatibility, and overload causes before choosing parts.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD VI^ENGINE COMPONENTS<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_engine_components_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>This is the main MSC work window: the engine is a set of separate components, each with its own installation and removal dependencies. It opens from vanilla vehicle mechanics; right-click Engine → Inspect engine components is an additional route if it did not open automatically.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>The component window opens with vehicle mechanics and an open hood; use Inspect engine components on Engine only to reopen it. Right-click installed parts to remove or empty slots to install a carried part. Tools are mandatory; Mechanics changes success and damage risk rather than blocking work, and the tooltip shows tools, recommended skill, and removal order.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD VIII^WORKSHOP LIFT<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_engine_lift_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>A lift does more than speed up work: it turns the engine into a detachable assembly for deep service or swaps. This special operation belongs to the Engine context menu, not the ordinary component list.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>At a complete lift, stop the engine, open the hood, equip a wrench, then right-click Engine → Remove engine at lift or Install engine from lift. Removal places the same assembly on the lift, where it can be inspected and serviced before another car receives it. An empty engine bay stays empty; a cross-family swap works but carries compatibility stress.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD III^ROADSIDE REPAIRS<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_roadside_repair_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Roadside repair is a short reprieve to reach a workshop, not a complete restoration. Tape, wire, and tools apply to only three components, so use the option carefully.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>With hood open and engine stopped, right-click coolant hoses, fan belt, or ignition coil → Roadside repair. Hoses need duct tape and a screwdriver; the belt needs a wrench; the coil needs wire, tape, and a screwdriver. Repairs are temporary, top out at 60%, and give less benefit after repeats; only hoses can be saved from 0% condition.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD II^FLUID SERVICE<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_fluid_service_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Fluids are service resources: they can be drained, mixed, or contaminated. The correct liquid supports its system; a wrong one remains in the reservoir and spoils the mixture.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>In the component window, right-click Oil Pan, Radiator, or Transmission → Manage Fluids. Fill and drain with carried containers; fluids mix, so a wrong liquid remains inside and lowers system purity. Automatic gearboxes need ATF, while manuals need manual transmission oil.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD V^STARTING & CHARGING<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_starting_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Starting and charging are separate jobs. Battery and starter begin the engine; alternator and belt return charge while it runs. A car can start without an alternator but cannot run electrical loads for long.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>In Components, check battery, starter, alternator, and fan belt separately. Battery and starter crank the engine; the alternator charges only while its belt turns. A car can start without an alternator, but its battery drains under electrical load and a running engine stops when charge reaches zero.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD IX^TRANSMISSION SETUP<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_transmission_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>A gearbox transfers power only through the matching coupling. Automatic and manual systems are complete pairs, not interchangeable loose parts: a wrong pair lets the engine run but gives wheels no power.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Right-click Transmission or Power Coupling in Components. Remove the gearbox and old coupling before changing configuration, then install automatic + torque converter or manual + clutch. A wrong or missing pair lets the engine start but sends no power to wheels; wrong or dirty fluid causes slip, heat, and accelerated wear.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD XIII^PUSH VEHICLE<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_pushing_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>Pushing is an emergency way to move a stalled or obstructing car. A heavy vehicle and exhausted character require more effort, while higher Fitness preserves endurance.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>Leave an empty stationary vehicle and stand at its front or rear; right-click it → Push vehicle, or use the bound hotkey. Strength 3 only unlocks the action: more Strength creates a stronger shove and makes it cheaper, while Fitness reduces endurance cost. Heavy vehicles are harder, shown as Effort in the tooltip. Exhaustion blocks pushing and a brief recovery prevents spam.

<type:parent, width:800, height:1000><type:texture, x:0, y:0, width:800, height:1000, r:0.73, g:0.69, b:0.57, a:1><type:texture, x:32, y:32, width:736, height:936, r:0.15, g:0.12, b:0.08, a:1><type:texture, x:38, y:38, width:724, height:924, r:0.88, g:0.85, b:0.74, a:1><type:text, x:75, y:78, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.72, scaleY:0.72, font:SdfOldBold>MASKARAD VII^REBUILD & SALVAGE<type:texture, x:100, y:200, texture:media/textures/MSC/printmedia_workshop_rebuild_640.png, width:600, height:300><type:text, x:105, y:540, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.38, scaleY:0.38, autoWidth:1500, font:SdfOldRegular>A removed component is not always scrap. Dismantle it for its material family or rebuild it while retaining exact class and repair history. This makes workshop parts valuable.<type:text, x:105, y:680, r:0.28, g:0.18, b:0.08, a:1, scaleX:0.48, scaleY:0.48, font:SdfOldBold>IN GAME<type:text, x:105, y:725, r:0.12, g:0.08, b:0.04, a:1, scaleX:0.40, scaleY:0.40, autoWidth:1450, font:SdfOldRegular>For a removed component, use its inventory actions Dismantle or Repair. Dismantling accepts components at 30% condition or higher and turns them into the matching material family; healthier parts yield more. Rebuilding needs a work surface, light, tools, and two matching materials. Normal parts repair less effectively each time; legendary parts do not.
Brochure XIV: heating and A/C requirements.
Brochure X: component fit classes and mismatch stress.
Brochure IV: cooling-loop failures and overheating.
Brochure I: use a dipstick to reveal oil, coolant, and transmission-fluid quality.
Brochure XII: vehicle overload while driving.
Brochure VI: inspect, remove, and install engine components.
Brochure VIII: complete engine-assembly work at the lift.
Brochure III: temporary repair of hoses, belt, and ignition coil.
Brochure II: fill and drain the three vehicle fluid containers.
Brochure V: starting battery, starter, alternator, and belt.
Brochure IX: correct gearbox and coupling pairs.
Brochure XIII: Strength, Fitness, mass, exhaustion, and cooldown when pushing a vehicle.
Brochure VII: dismantle and rebuild removed parts.
Allows a shove near either end of a vehicle's side to turn it. Front and rear pushing remains available when disabled.
Multiplies condition loss from normal running wear and fluid-related engine damage. Zero disables those MSC wear sources.
Chance that each newly generated component belongs to a different Standard, Heavy-Duty, or Sport class. The transmission pair always stays internally consistent.
Multiplies condition- and pressure-related oil, coolant, and transmission-fluid leaks. Zero disables MSC leaks.
Controls how often oil, coolant, and transmission-fluid bottles appear as loot. 0 disables them, 1 is the default rate, and 2 doubles it.
Controls how often Heavy-Duty parts appear as loot. 0 disables them, 1 is the default rate, and 2 doubles it.
Legendary chance for newly created MSC components. Lower values make legendary parts more common; 350 means one chance in 350.
Shifts newly initialized vehicles toward better or worse coherent engine loadouts. Only affects vehicles initialized after the setting is applied.
Chance that a newly initialized vehicle receives a manual transmission and clutch instead of an automatic transmission and torque converter.
Controls how many components may be absent from newly initialized vehicles. Optional and service parts are more likely to be missing than critical internals.
Controls how often Sport parts appear as loot. 0 disables them, 1 is the default rate, and 2 doubles it.
Controls how often Standard parts appear as loot. 0 disables them, 1 is the default rate, and 2 doubles it.
